core_obligations: One direction (proof lines 10562-10575): given G on S with nonvanishing degree n cohomology, its pullback g^{-1}G on X has nonvanishing cohomology in the same degree, because the composite of the pullback and the pushforward is multiplication by the degree of the covering, which is prime to l and hence invertible on l-power torsion coefficients.

The other direction (proof lines 10575-10596): conversely, for F on X with nonvanishing cohomology the author descends the class to some X_i using the limit description, and then pushes it forward to S, which again uses the invertibility of the degree to keep the class nonzero.
Both directions are stated in the form given in the last sentence of the statement, with the transfers exhibited explicitly.
proof_roadmap: Use that pullback followed by pushforward is multiplication by the degree, coprime to l.
Show that nonvanishing transfers in either direction along the limit of prime-to-l covers.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the nonvanishing of degree n cohomology with l-power torsion coefficients is the same on S and on the limit X of a directed system of finite etale S-schemes of constant degree prime to l (statement lines 10542-10560). The proof uses that the composite of pullback and pushforward along such a cover is multiplication by the degree, which is invertible on l-power torsion coefficients, in one direction directly (proof lines 10562-10575) and in the other direction after descending the class to a finite stage through the limit description (proof lines 10575-10596). The non-formal content is the descent of a cohomology class from the limit to a stage. The claim is H2: two applications of the same transfer argument.
